name: Alliance High School
description: One of Kenya's oldest and most prestigious national secondary schools for boys, established by the Alliance of Protestant Churches in 1926. Located in Kikuyu, Kiambu County.

name: Alliance Girls High School
description: A leading national girls' secondary school in Kikuyu, Kiambu County, founded in 1948 and consistently ranked among Kenya's top-performing schools.

name: Mang'u High School
description: A historic Catholic-founded national boys' secondary school near Thika, established in 1925 and known for strong academic and STEM performance.

name: Starehe Boys' Centre
description: A renowned national boys' school and charitable institution in Nairobi, founded in 1959, known for giving opportunities to bright students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

name: Kenya High School
description: One of Kenya's oldest national girls' schools, founded in 1910 in Nairobi, with a long history of academic excellence.

name: Nairobi School
description: Formerly the Prince of Wales School, Nairobi School is a national boys' secondary school established in 1929, one of the oldest in the country.

name: Lenana School
description: Formerly the Duke of York School, Lenana School is a national boys' secondary school in Nairobi founded in 1948.

name: Maseno School
description: Founded in 1906 by the Church Missionary Society, Maseno School is the oldest secondary school in Kenya, located near Kisumu.

name: Friends School Kamusinga
description: A national boys' secondary school founded by Quaker missionaries in 1903, located in Webuye, Bungoma County.

name: Moi Girls High School Nairobi
description: A national girls' secondary school in Nairobi, founded in 1962, known for consistently strong national examination performance.

name: Precious Blood Riruta
description: A Catholic-founded girls' secondary school in Riruta, Nairobi, recognised as one of the top-performing extra-county schools in Kenya.

name: Loreto High School Limuru
description: A national Catholic girls' secondary school established by the Loreto Sisters in 1928, located in Limuru, Kiambu County.

name: Cardinal Otunga High School
description: A Catholic-founded extra-county boys' secondary school in Mosocho, Kisii County, named after Cardinal Maurice Otunga.

name: Kakamega High School
description: A long-established national boys' secondary school in Kakamega town, one of the oldest schools in western Kenya.

name: St. Mary's School Yala
description: A Catholic-founded extra-county boys' secondary school in Yala, Siaya County, established in 1939.

name: Brookhouse School
description: A private international school in Karen, Nairobi, founded in 1981, offering the British IGCSE and A-Level curricula with both day and boarding options.

name: Hillcrest International School
description: A private day school in Karen, Nairobi, founded in 1964, offering the IGCSE curriculum to a multicultural student body.

name: Nairobi Primary School
description: A long-established public primary school in Nairobi's city centre, offering the CBC curriculum to day scholars.

name: Kidogo Early Years
description: A network of community-based early childhood development micro-nurseries operating in Nairobi's informal settlements, supporting quality early years learning.

name: University of Nairobi
description: Kenya's oldest public university, tracing its origins to the Royal Technical College founded in 1956, chartered as a university in 1970.

name: Kenyatta University
description: A major public university in Kahawa, Nairobi, established in 1965 and chartered as a fully-fledged university in 1985.

name: Strathmore University
description: A private university in Nairobi that began as Strathmore College in 1961, gaining full university charter in 2008.

name: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology
description: A leading public university in Juja, Kiambu County, specialising in agriculture, engineering and technology, founded in 1981.
